resolved_findings.resolution: Removed the publicDisplayLabel(entryId) helper and its call site in registerWalkIn() entirely; the queue_entries INSERT no longer supplies a public_display_label value at all, relying solely on migration 0007's BEFORE INSERT trigger to assign it. loadRegistration()'s re-select is unchanged. Fixed by Claude (failover from ChatGPT's implementer capacity, which could not apply a surgical patch through its available write interface) as a narrow, minimal diff (3 insertions, 15 deletions in one file). Verified locally before push: typecheck/lint/format clean, full suite 52/52 (3 consecutive runs of the affected integration files) against real Postgres. Existing coverage in tests/integration/waiting-room-public.test.ts ('uses a public label that is independent from the queue-entry UUID') continues to pass, now for the right reason (no app-level ID-derived candidate is ever computed) rather than merely because the trigger overwrote one. CI green on this exact head (run 34065969197). Since Claude authored this SHA, Claude handed off to Gemini Chat for the non-author gate rather than self-gating.

Codex's automated review bot found a real gap in the CLAUDE-034 fix commit (independently confirmed by Claude before ChatGPT's formal CHANGES_REQUIRED handoff arrived): migration 0007's BEFORE INSERT trigger only governs future inserts, so any queue_entries row created before this migration runs would keep its pre-existing ID-derived public_display_label forever, meaning the new unauthenticated waiting-room snapshot could still publish ID-derived labels for upgraded/pre-existing data. Fixed by adding a one-time backfill block to migration 0007 that regenerates every existing row's label using the identical collision-safe random generation the trigger uses, scoped per session -- confirmed harmless no-op on a fresh/empty database. Added a real-Postgres regression test that disables the trigger, inserts a row with the exact pre-migration insecure label (simulating real historical data), re-enables the trigger, then re-runs the backfill logic directly and asserts the label is no longer ID-derived. Verified: full suite 53/53 (3 consecutive runs of the affected test file), typecheck/lint/format clean. CI green on this exact head (run 34066463561). Fixed by Claude; handed off to Gemini Chat for the non-author gate since Claude authored this SHA too.

service_order fully removed (column, index, every code reference) per ChatGPT's ARCHITECTURE_DECISION; priority_order is now the sole authoritative override using the pre-existing queue_entries_session_priority_uq index. call()/listOperational() order by priority_order-cohort-first then eligibility_order/registration_order, matching ARCHITECTURE.md:96-108. reorder()'s active cohort is state IN (waiting,checked_in) AND priority_order IS NOT NULL with correct 1..N+1 insert / 1..N move bound differentiation. Lifecycle exits (call/no_show/cancel) compact the remaining priority cohort to contiguous 1..N via the same NULL-first-then-assign pattern from CLAUDE-031, now correctly reused for priority_order in both reorder() and command()'s own compaction block. queue_order_version now advances on every cohort-affecting lifecycle command, not just reorder() (closing the standing Codex P1 finding from the first commit). UI removed all service_order references and forces an authoritative reload after every command/reorder instead of optimistic client-side sorting. Independently re-verified against real Postgres: 3 consecutive full-suite runs (34/34), typecheck/lint/format/unit+API clean, plus a fresh adversarial test inducing a priority-cohort gap via command()'s own compaction path and reordering through it -- succeeds, deterministic, no raw 23505. CI (run 34053605419) confirmed tied to this exact head, all green.
